text:
The tail current is the most likely culprit. Input-pair gm (about 325 µS) sets UGBW at roughly 25 MHz on the 2 pF load, which matches the simulated 24.7 MHz. Since the input pair is in weak inversion, its gm is set by its current rather than its width, so M1 and M2 are not the problem. The tail current is 30 µA, which matches the M5/M6 mirror ratio of about 3.0. That mirror is internally consistent, so the fault is most likely an undersized M5 (or an oversized M6) that sets the tail current too low for the 43 MHz target. The sensitivities support this: M5 and M6 have nearly symmetric effects on UGBW and settling, and both are driven by tail current. M5's low Vds-Vdsat margin (0.031 V) is a consequence of the low Vdsat from its small width, not an independent fault. M4 and M3 follow with smaller effects on UGBW.

This limits input-pair gm, so UGBW (24.7 MHz vs 43 MHz) and settling (55 ns vs 33 ns) fail. The low M5 Vds-Vdsat margin is a side effect of its small width."}
